topic: How much water a household really needs for 72 hours

content.hook: How much water does your household really need?

slides.title: How much *water* for *72 hours*?
slides.body: A simple sum. No panic, no pallets of bottles.

slides.title: Start with *3 litres* a day
slides.body: Per person, for drinking and basic cooking. It is a practical planning figure, in line with official guidance such as MSB and RCB.

slides.title: Three days means *9 litres* each
slides.body: 3 litres × 3 days = 9 litres per person. Family of four? 36 litres. That is six 6-litre bottles.

slides.title: Some people need *more*
slides.body: Babies, hot weather, pets and anyone unwell may need extra. Treat 9 litres as a minimum and add a margin.

slides.title: Store it *smart*
slides.body: Use clean, sealed bottles. Keep them somewhere cool and dark. Check dates once or twice a year.

slides.title: Apartment? Think *weight and spread*
slides.body: Water is heavy and lifts may not work. Spread bottles across a few cupboards instead of one big stack.

slides.title: Do it in *one evening*
slides.body: Count your household, do the sum, buy the bottles, write the date on them. Done. Then you can stop thinking about it.

slides.title: The full 72-hour list, *ready to tick off*

content.caption:
Water is the one thing people overthink and under-prepare.

Here is the calm version.

Plan for about 3 litres per person per day. That covers drinking and basic cooking. Over 72 hours, that is 9 litres each.

A family of four: 36 litres. Not a bunker. Just a few bottles in a cupboard.

Then add a margin. Babies, hot weather, pets and anyone unwell may need more. When in doubt, store a little extra.

Keep it simple:
• Clean, sealed bottles
• Cool, dark place
• Check dates once or twice a year
• In an apartment, spread the weight across a few cupboards

That is the whole job. One evening, and it is off your mind.

Ready72h is a household preparedness planner for the first 72 hours of a crisis. It is based on official guidance from Sweden's MSB, Germany's BBK and Poland's RCB. It includes a full supply checklist: water, food, medicine, cash and communications. This is a safety topic, not a place to profit off anxiety.
